idea-plugin.name: spek - OpenSpec Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
spek is an OpenSpec content viewer that lets you browse specs, changes, and task progress directly within your IDE.

Features:

  • Specs Browser — Browse spec documents with BDD syntax highlighting (WHEN/GIVEN, THEN, AND, MUST/SHALL)
  • Changes Browser — View changes with a tab per artifact the change contains (custom OpenSpec schemas supported), with the change's schema shown as a badge; rows surface creation/archive dates and lifecycle duration
  • Timeline — Horizontal Gantt-style chart of every change's lifecycle, with optional spec-topic grouping and an auto-scaling time axis
  • Task Progress — Track task completion with section-grouped progress bars
  • Graph View — Interactive force-directed graph showing spec-change relationships
  • Full-text Search — Search across all specs and changes
  • Spec Diff — Compare current spec content against historical change versions
  • Live Reload — Automatically refreshes when openspec files change on disk
  • Collapsible Tree Navigator — A Specs / Changes tree sits above the viewer. Hide it from the tool window title bar or the gear menu to give the viewer the whole tool window; the choice and the split ratio are remembered per project
  • Dark / Light Theme — Syncs with your IDE theme

Supported IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, and other IntelliJ-based IDEs (2023.3+)

Getting Started: Open a project that contains an openspec/ directory. The spek tool window will appear in the right sidebar.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.13.0

A requirement is now called what it is named. Every requirement heading in a spec opened with the word Requirement: and every scenario with Scenario: — the same twelve characters at the front of every heading in the document, taken from exactly where a reader scans for what distinguishes one from the next. Suggested from this tool window (issue #42), which is where the cost is plainest: at a few hundred pixels of width, the boilerplate stays and the distinguishing part is what truncates.

  • Requirement and scenario headings drop their format keyword, in the rendered spec and in its table of contents. This became removable only in 1.12.0: before the ADDED Requirements label was restored to visibility, the keyword was the only thing naming what these sections were. Presentation only — your files, every heading id and every deep link are untouched.
  • The rule beside an open section now marks that section. Consecutive requirements drew rules that met, forming a single unbroken line down the whole page: a bracket around everything says the same as no bracket at all. Each requirement now carries its own, ending where the requirement ends. A nested open scenario no longer draws a second rule of equal weight beside its parent's.
  • Expanding a scenario no longer nudges the rest of the page. The gap between sections depended on what the last visible element inside one happened to be, so opening a scenario pushed every requirement below it down by a further 8px.
  • A little more room around the fold — the body sits further from the rule, and the disclosure arrow is no longer drawn against it.
